#### Native C++ route

The recipe above prototypes a reconstruction in Python and selects a built-in one by name; it stays the one
recipe. A new scheme that the solver itself runs is a C++ class, built into the library and selected from the YAML
card, and this route is the one place that says how, for a reconstruction and for a Riemann solver. Each step below
is a fact of the code at the pin.

**Select it from YAML.** A reconstruction is read from `dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` for $x_1$ and from
`dynamics/reconstruct/horizontal` for $x_2$ and $x_3$ ([`src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp:24-27`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp#L24-L27)). Each section takes `shock`, `type` and
`scale`; `type` defaults to `dc` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:31-36`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L31-L36)):

```cpp
  check_keys(node[section], "dynamics/reconstruct/" + section,
             {"shock", "type", "scale"});
  op->shock() = node[section]["shock"].as<bool>(false);
  op->interp() = InterpOptionsImpl::create();
  op->interp()->type() = node[section]["type"].as<std::string>("dc");
  op->interp()->scale() = node[section]["scale"].as<bool>(false);
```

A Riemann solver is read from `dynamics/riemann-solver`, whose keys are `type` and `dir` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:18-19`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L18-L19)).
A section without `type` gives `roe` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:27-28`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L27-L28)):

```cpp
  op->type() = node["type"].as<std::string>("roe");
  op->dir() = node["dir"].as<std::string>("omni");
```

A card with no such section keeps the options as created ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:17`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L17)), whose default is another solver,
`hllc` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp:33`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp#L33)):

```cpp
  if (!config[section]["riemann-solver"]) return op;
  ADD_ARG(std::string, type) = "hllc";
```

**Lookup.** The name is compared as a string, branch by branch, in `InterpImpl::create` and
`RiemannSolverImpl::create`; there is no table and no suffix added to the name. A name with no branch is refused
when the block is built ([`src/recon/interpolation.cpp:38`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/interpolation.cpp#L38), [`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:69`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L69)):

```cpp
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "Interp: unknown type " + opts->type());
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "RiemannSolver: unknown type " + opts->type());
```

A reconstruction module is created twice, under the names `interp1` and `interp2` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:75-76`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L75-L76)):

```cpp
  pinterp1 = InterpImpl::create(options->interp(), this, "interp1");
  pinterp2 = InterpImpl::create(options->interp(), this, "interp2");
```

and for `weno3` and `weno5` the last character of that name chooses the class ([`src/recon/interpolation.cpp:29-36`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/interpolation.cpp#L29-L36)):

```cpp
  } else if (opts->type() == "weno5") {
    if (name.back() == '1') {
      return p->register_module(name, Weno5Interp(opts));
    } else if (name.back() == '2') {
      return p->register_module(name, Center5Interp(opts));

```

**Write the class.** The header `src/recon/interpolation.hpp` declares `InterpImpl`, the base of every
reconstruction. Its `forward` sizes the two outputs from `stencils()` and fills them through `left` and `right`
([`src/recon/interpolation.hpp:73-89`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/interpolation.hpp#L73-L89)):

```cpp
  virtual std::pair<torch::Tensor, torch::Tensor> forward(
      torch::Tensor w, int dim,
      torch::optional<torch::Tensor> wl = torch::nullopt,
      torch::optional<torch::Tensor> wr = torch::nullopt) {
    auto vec = w.sizes().vec();
    vec[dim] -= stencils() - 1;  // reduce size by stencils - 1

    auto wlv = wl.value_or(torch::empty(vec, w.options()));
    auto wrv = wr.value_or(torch::empty(vec, w.options()));

    left(w, dim, wlv);
    right(w, dim, wrv);

    wl = wlv;
    wr = wrv;
    return std::make_pair(wlv, wrv);
  }
```

The donor-cell class is the smallest one to follow ([`src/recon/interpolation.hpp:101-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/interpolation.hpp#L101-L120)):

```cpp
class DonorCellInterpImpl : public torch::nn::Cloneable<DonorCellInterpImpl>,
                            public InterpImpl {
 public:
  //! Constructor to initialize the layer
  DonorCellInterpImpl() = default;
  explicit DonorCellInterpImpl(InterpOptions const& options_)
      : InterpImpl(options_) {
    reset();
  }
  void reset() override {}
  using InterpImpl::forward;

  void left(torch::Tensor w, int dim, torch::Tensor const& out) override {
    out.copy_(w.slice(dim, 0, w.size(dim)));
  }
  void right(torch::Tensor w, int dim, torch::Tensor const& out) override {
    out.copy_(w.slice(dim, 0, w.size(dim) - 1));
  }
};
TORCH_MODULE(DonorCellInterp);
```

A Riemann solver derives from `RiemannSolverImpl`, declared in `src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp`
([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp:97-117`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp#L97-L117)):

```cpp
class RoeSolverImpl : public torch::nn::Cloneable<RoeSolverImpl>,
                      public RiemannSolverImpl {
 public:
  //! Constructor to initialize the layers
  RoeSolverImpl() = default;
  explicit RoeSolverImpl(const RiemannSolverOptions& options_,
                         torch::nn::Module* p = nullptr)
      : RiemannSolverImpl(options_, p) {
    reset();
  }
  void reset() override;

  //! Solver the Riemann problem
  torch::Tensor forward(torch::Tensor wl, torch::Tensor wr, int dim,
                        torch::Tensor out,
                        torch::Tensor face_pressure = torch::Tensor()) override;

 protected:
  FORWARD_HAS_DEFAULT_ARGS({4, torch::nn::AnyValue(torch::Tensor())})
};
TORCH_MODULE(RoeSolver);
```

Add one branch to the matching `create`, as for `dc` ([`src/recon/interpolation.cpp:11-12`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/interpolation.cpp#L11-L12)) and `roe` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:56-57`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L56-L57)):

```cpp
  if (opts->type() == "dc") {
    return p->register_module(name, DonorCellInterp(opts));
  if (opts->type() == "roe") {
    return p->register_module(name, RoeSolver(opts, p));
```

**Files.** Every `.cpp` file in `src/recon/` and `src/riemann/` is compiled into the library
([`src/CMakeLists.txt:42-43`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/CMakeLists.txt#L42-L43)), and with CUDA every `.cu` file there ([`src/CMakeLists.txt:128-129`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/CMakeLists.txt#L128-L129)); a new file there needs no CMake edit.

**Face slots: which state is left and which is right.** The two slots of the reconstruction result are named
by this enum ([`src/snap.h:44-45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/snap.h#L44-L45)):

```cpp
  ILT = 0,  //!< Left interface
  IRT = 1,  //!< Right interface
```

Face $i$ is the face on the low side of cell $i$, between cells $i-1$ and $i$. The reconstruction hands the method
two slices of the result ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:54-57`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L54-L57)):

```cpp
  auto outl = wlr[IRT].slice(dim, il - 1, iu + 1);
  auto outr = wlr[ILT].slice(dim, il, iu + 2);

  pinterp->forward(w, dim, outl, outr);
```

so `left`, the value at each cell's low-side face, lands in slot `IRT` at the cell's own index, and `right`, the
value at each cell's high-side face, lands in slot `ILT` one index on. At index $i$, slot `ILT` holds the state
on the left of face $i$, from cell $i-1$, and slot `IRT` the state on its right, from cell $i$; the donor-cell
`left` and `right` above and step 5 of the recipe show exactly this. The solver takes slot `ILT` as `wl` and slot
`IRT` as `wr` ([`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:583`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L583)), and its flux at index $i$ is the flux through face $i$: the update of cell $i$ uses
the fluxes at $i$ and $i+1$ ([`src/coord/coordinate.cpp:732-734`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L732-L734)):

```cpp
    dflx.slice(DIM1, si, ei) +=
        face_area1(si + 1, ei + 1) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si + 1, ei + 1) -
        face_area1(si, ei) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si, ei);
```

**Riemann shapes and face pressure.** The flux and the face pressure of $x_1$ are float64 buffers of the full
block, ghosts included: the flux has one row per variable, the face pressure one row only, and neither exists
when the block has one cell along $x_1$ ([`src/hydro/hydro.cpp:189-197`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L189-L197)):

```cpp
  if (nc1 > 1) {
    _flux1 = register_buffer(
        "F1", torch::zeros({nvar, nc3, nc2, nc1}, torch::kFloat64));
    _face_pressure1 =
        register_buffer("P1", torch::zeros({nc3, nc2, nc1}, torch::kFloat64));
  } else {
    _flux1 = register_buffer("F1", torch::Tensor());
    _face_pressure1 = register_buffer("P1", torch::Tensor());
  }
```

The left and right states have the shape of the state, as the reconstruction result above has. The solver writes
the face pressure into the tensor it is given, or into a scratch tensor of one row when it is given none
([`src/riemann/roe.cpp:47-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/roe.cpp#L47-L48)):

```cpp
  auto face_pressure_out =
      face_pressure.defined() ? face_pressure : torch::empty_like(wl[IDN]);
```

Only the $x_1$ call passes the face pressure, and not with the shallow-water EOS ([`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:580-582`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L580-L582)); the $x_2$ and
$x_3$ calls pass none ([`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:827`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L827), [`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:859`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L859)):

```cpp
      auto face_pressure1 = options->eos()->type() == "shallow-water"
                                ? torch::Tensor()
                                : _face_pressure1;
      priemann->forward(wlr2[ILT], wlr2[IRT], DIM2, _flux2);
      priemann->forward(wlr3[ILT], wlr3[IRT], DIM3, _flux3);
```

A solver that keeps the base `forward` refuses a defined face pressure ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:42-45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L42-L45)), so a hydro run with
it stops at the first $x_1$ call, as the built-in `upwind` does; a solver for the hydro overrides `forward` and
writes the face pressure:

```cpp
  TORCH_CHECK(
      !face_pressure.defined(),
      "Face-pressure output is not implemented for Riemann solver type ",
      options->type());
```

The face pressure is read by the gnomonic-equiangle geometry ([`src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp:441`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L441)) and by the spherical-polar one
with the exact $x_1$ centroid ([`src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp:252`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L252)); the base geometry ignores it ([`src/coord/coordinate.cpp:786`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L786)).

**Shapes, outputs and device.**

- Reconstruction output: the result is allocated like the input, so it has the input's dtype and device, and the
  method writes into it ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:88`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L88)):

  ```cpp
    auto result = torch::zeros(vec, w.options());
  ```

- Riemann call: the solver gets the left and right states from the reconstruction, each of the shape of the state
  (the result above is the state's shape with 2 prepended), the direction, and the flux tensor to fill
  ([`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:583`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L583)):

  ```cpp
        priemann->forward(wlr1[ILT], wlr1[IRT], DIM1, _flux1, face_pressure1);
  ```

- In place, one dtype: the solver writes the flux into its fourth argument without resizing it, and all tensors
  must share one dtype ([`src/riemann/roe.cpp:52-63`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/roe.cpp#L52-L63)):

  ```cpp
    auto iter = at::TensorIteratorConfig()
                    .resize_outputs(false)
                    .check_all_same_dtype(true)
                    .declare_static_shape(flx.sizes(), /*squash_dims=*/0)
                    .add_output(flx)
                    .add_owned_output(face_pressure_out.unsqueeze(0))
                    .add_input(wl)
                    .add_input(wr)
                    .add_input(elr)
                    .add_input(glr)
                    .add_input(clr)
                    .build();
  ```

- Device: the kernel is chosen by the device of the flux tensor ([`src/riemann/roe.cpp:65`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/roe.cpp#L65)):

  ```cpp
    at::native::call_roe(flx.device().type(), iter, dim, ideal_moist, nvapor,
  ```

- Ownership: `create` registers the new module as a submodule of its parent with `register_module`
  ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:56-57`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L56-L57)); the solver keeps only a non-owning pointer back to its hydro ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp:64-65`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp#L64-L65)):

  ```cpp
    //! non-owning reference to parent
    HydroImpl const* phydro = nullptr;
  ```

**Rebuild.** Build the library ([`README.md:96-97`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/README.md#L96-L97)) and reinstall the Python package ([`README.md:100-102`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/README.md#L100-L102)):

```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DNETCDF=ON
cmake --build build --parallel 3
pip install .
```

Then set the new name as `type` under `dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` or `horizontal`, or under
`dynamics/riemann-solver`.

**Check the registration.** This test builds a block from the repository deck with the names selected, and fails
when a name has no branch in `create`. Run it from the repository root with the rebuilt package, with the new
names in place of `weno5` and `lmars`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import snapy
import yaml

def selects(recon, riemann):
    """Build a block selecting these names; raises if one is unknown."""
    deck = yaml.safe_load(Path("examples/straka_single.yaml").read_text())
    deck["dynamics"]["reconstruct"] = {
        "vertical": {"type": recon},
        "horizontal": {"type": recon},
    }
    deck["dynamics"]["riemann-solver"] = {"type": riemann}
    Path("check.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(deck))
    options = snapy.MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml("check.yaml")
    return snapy.MeshBlock(options)

selects("weno5", "lmars")
try:
    selects("weno5", "mine")
except RuntimeError as err:
    assert "RiemannSolver: unknown type mine" in str(err)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an unregistered name was accepted")
print("N6 scheme: the selected names are registered")
```
